n: Palayam St. Gregorios Orthodox Chapel
ds:
105 students (2025) - established under the visionary leadership of L.L. H.G. Philipose Mar Theophilos in 1975, this MGOCSM hub became a flagship model of ecclesial youth infrastructure. The first warden, Rev. Dn. George Kurien (later H.G. Geevarghese Mar Coorilos), oversaw its transformation from a repurposed residence into a full-fledged student and spiritual centre, with a chapel, auditorium, and guest facilities.

The landmark consecration of the expanded complex in 1977 by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews I, with international ecumenical presence, marked its rise as a theological and communal node within the urban Orthodox milieu.

n: Palayam St. Peter's Orthodox Church
ds:
0 families (2025) - established in 1975 amidst ecclesial realignment, this parish emerged as a distinct patriarchal congregation in Kerala’s capital, with its edifice consecrated on 13–14 February 1982 by Patriarch Ignatius Zakka I Iwas. Governed by a schismatic constitution (1979), it now comprises over 250 Patriarchal families (2025), and administers multiple charitable institutions, including a special-needs school, two cemeteries, and a cross shrine in Pongumoodu elevated to parish status in 2003.

Historical Footnote: The first leader of this schismatic congregation was a lay acolyte, hastily ordained within four months without seminary formation—an act widely condemned as a serious breach of ecclesial discipline.

n: Vadakkankulam St. Thomas Malankara Orthodox Church

n: Palayam St. George Orthodox Cathedral
ds:
1,916 families (2022) - consecrated in 1900 by Saint Gregorios of Parumala, this cathedral, elevated on June 23, 1991, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II as the episcopal seat of the Trivandrum Diocese, constitutes the largest urban parish within the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, encompassing over 3,000 regularly attending family.

There are four weekly Holy Qurbanas, three additionally monthly services, as well as thirteen active prayer groups under this parish.

Prominent Members: K.J. Yesudas (most famous singer from Kerala, married at this parish, later converted to Hinduism)

Historical Footnote: Established as the first Syrian Christian parish in Thiruvananthapuram district, this church serves as the historical progenitor of all subsequent Marthomite, Malankara Catholic, and schismatic Neo-Jacobite communities in the Thiruvananthapuram Capital Region.

n: Puthoor St. Kuriakose Orthodox Church
ds: 0 families (2025) - established in 1918 as a chapel, this church was consecrated in 1928 by H.G. Michael Mar Dionysius. It currently houses the sacred relics of St. Kuriakose the Martyr and has a membership of 56 schismatic families (2018).

n: Sooranad North St. Mary's Salem Orthodox Church
ds:
81 families (2022) - The Orthodox faithful residing in and around Sooranad North, particularly near the Government High School and Kannamam Market area, were for many years members of their mother parishes—St. Thomas Orthodox Church and St. Mary's Orthodox Church, Sooranad. Due to the difficulty of travelling long distances to attend Holy Qurbana and other liturgical services, the need for a new parish gradually became evident. A plot of land, adjacent to St. Thomas U.P. School, owned by the Church, was graciously made available. After obtaining the necessary permissions, construction of the new church was initiated by dismantling an old structure within the school premises.

On 22 November 1968, under the leadership Fr. T.G. Geevarghese, the faithful formally entered the church premises. The foundation stone of the church was laid on 28 November 1968. The parish was officially established in January 1969. The consecration ceremonies were completed on 30 and 31 January 1969. Rev. Fr. T. G. Geevarghese was appointed as the first Vicar, and the parish was named St. Mary's Salem Orthodox Syrian Church, Sooranad North. Subsequently, the parish committee and various spiritual organizations were formed. From February 1969 onward, regular Holy Qurbana and worship services were conducted.

പരിശുദ്ധ പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ തിരുശേഷിപ്പിനാൽ ധന്യമായ ആഗോള പൗരസ്ത്യ ജോർജ്ജിയൻ തീർത്ഥാടന കേന്ദ്രം:

എ.ഡി 1915 ഒക്ടോബര്‍ മാസത്തില്‍ ബഥേല്‍ സെന്റ്‌ ജോര്‍ജ്ജ്‌ പള്ളി എന്ന നാമധേയത്തില്‍ ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ പണി തുടങ്ങി 1916 ജനുവരി മാസത്തില്‍ ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ കൂദാശാ കര്‍മ്മം കാലം ചെയ്‌ത ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ കാതോലിക്കാ ബാവാ തിരുമേനി നടത്തി. പ്രസ്തുത ദേവാലയം 1919 ജൂലൈ മാസത്തില്‍ ഉണ്ടായ കാറ്റും മഴയും മൂലം ഇടിഞ്ഞുവീണു. പെട്ടെന്ന്‌ അതേ സ്ഥാനത്ത്‌ തന്നെ ദൈവാലയം പണിതു.

പുതിയ മദ്ബഹായുടെ പണി 1952 ഒക്ടോബര്‍ മാസത്തില്‍ ആരംഭിച്ചു. അതിന്റെ ഉത്തരനിരപ്പു വരെയുള്ള കെട്ട്‌ 1963-ല്‍ പൂര്‍ത്തിയായി. ഈ ഭിത്തി 12-7-1963-ല്‍ ഉണ്ടായ അതിഭയങ്കരമായ മഴ നിമിത്തം ഇടിഞ്ഞു വീഴുകയുണ്ടായി. വീണ്ടും അതേ പ്ലാനില്‍ തന്നെ ഒരു മദ്ബഹാ പണിയണമെന്നുള്ള പൊതു യോഗ തീരുമാനമനുസരിച്ച്‌ 22-8-1963-ല്‍ റവ, വൈദ്യന്‍ യോശുവ കത്തനാര്‍ അവര്‍കളാല്‍ ശിലാസ്ഥാപനം നടത്തപ്പെടുകയും തുടര്‍ന്ന്‌ പണി നടത്തപ്പെടുകയും ചെയ്തു 1971-ല്‍ പുതിയ പള്ളിയുടെ പണി ആരംഭിച്ചു. പുതിയ ദേവാലയത്തിന്‌ പോര്‍ച്ച്‌ ഉള്‍പ്പടെ 90 അടിനീളവും 27 അടി വീതിയുമുണ്ട്‌. ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ കൂദാശ 1985 ജനുവരി 9, 10 തീയതികളില്‍ മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മാര്‍ത്തോമ്മ മാത്യൂസ്‌ പ്രഥമന്‍ കാതോലിക്കാ ബാവായുടെ പ്രധാന കാര്‍മ്മികത്വത്തിലും, മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മാര്‍ത്തോമ്മ മാത്യൂസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ കതോലിക്കാ ബാവയുടേയും (അന്ന്‌ നിയുക്ത കാതോലിക്കാ), അഭി.ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ലീസ്‌ മാര്‍ ദീയസ്‌കോറസ്‌ തിരുമേനിയുടെ സഹകരണത്തിലും നടത്തി.

ദൈവാലയത്തിന്റെ സ്ഥലപരിമിതി മനസ്സിലാക്കി ഇരുവശങ്ങള്‍ വീതി കൂട്ടുകയും, അതിനോടനുബന്ധിച്ച്‌ രണ്ട്‌ മദ്ബഹാകള്‍ നിര്‍മ്മിക്കുകയും ചെയ്തു, കുര്‍ബാന അനുഷ്ഠിക്കുവാന്‍ 5 ബലി പീഠങ്ങളുമുണ്ട്‌.

പരിശുദ്ധ ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ സഹദായുടെ അതിശ്രേഷ്ഠമായ മദ്ധ്യസ്ഥതയുള്ള ഈ ദൈവാലയത്തെ, പൗരസ്ത്യ കാതോലിക്കായും, മലങ്കര മെത്രാ പോലീത്തയുമായ മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മര്‍ത്തോമ്മ പൗലോസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ തിരുമനസ്സുകൊണ്ട്‌ നമ്പർ 39/2011 കല്പന പ്രകാരം നല്ലില സെന്റ് ജോർജ് ഓർത്തഡോക്സ് തീർത്ഥാടന പള്ളി എന്ന പേരിൽ ജോർജ്ജിയൻ തീർത്ഥാടന കേന്ദ്രമായി ഉയർത്തപെട്ടു. 2011 മെയ്‌ 2-ാം തീയതി തീർത്ഥാടന പ്രഖ്യാപനം സമ്മേളനം നടത്തപ്പെട്ടു.

പരിശുദ്ധ എപ്പിസ്‌ക്കോപ്പന്‍ സുന്നഹദോസ്‌ ഇടവകയുടെ അപേക്ഷ പരിഗണിച്ച്‌ നമ്പര്‍ HES/HH/75/2011 കല്പന പ്രകാരം നവംബര്‍ മാസം 11-ാം തീയതി പരിശുദ്ധ പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ തിരു ശേഷിപ്പ് അഭിവന്ദ്യ സഖറിയാ മാര്‍ അന്തോണിയോസ്‌ മെത്രാപൊലീത്താ തിരുമനസ്സിന്റേയും അഭിവന്ദ്യ പൗലോസ്‌ മാര്‍ പക്കോമിയോസ്‌ തിരുമനസ്സിന്റേയും പ്രധാന കാര്‍മ്മികത്വത്തില്‍ പ്രതിഷ്ഠിക്കുകയുണ്ടായി എല്ലാ മാസവും 2-ാം ശനിയാഴ്ച ജോര്‍ജജിയന്‍ ധ്യാനവും എല്ലാ 4-ാം ശനിയാഴ്ച സന്ധ്യ നമസ്ക്കാരത്തിനു ശേഷം പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ നാമത്തിൽ മദ്ധ്യസ്ഥ പ്രാര്‍ത്ഥനയും നടത്തുന്നു.

ഇപ്പോൾ ഈ ദൈവാലയത്തിൽ 435 ഭവനങ്ങൾ ഉണ്ട്. 12 കുരിശടികളും, ഒരേക്കർ 34 സെന്റ് വസ്തു വും, പള്ളിയോട് ചേർന്ന് ഒരു പാഴ്സനേജും ഉണ്ട്. പള്ളിയുടെ ചുമതലയിൽ ബഥേൽ ഇംഗ്ലീഷ് മീഡിയം സ്കൂൾ എന്ന പേരിൽ ഒരു സ്കൂളും പ്രവർത്തിച്ചു വരുന്നു. സഭയിലെ എല്ലാ ആത്മീയ സംഘടനകളും, ഇടവകയിലെ ഭവനങ്ങളെ 8 വാർഡുകളായി വിഭജിച്ച് പ്രാർഥനായോഗങ്ങളും നടന്നുവരുന്നു. ഇപ്പോൾ ഇടവകയിൽ 5 പട്ടക്കാരും മരുമക്കളായ 5 പട്ടക്കാരും ഉണ്ട്. ഫാ. ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ്, മത്തായി, ഫാ. വി.കെ. ഡാനിയേൽ, ഫാ. , ജോഷം വൈദ്യൻ, ഫാ. പി.എം. ജോർജ്ജ്, അലക്സാണ്ടർ, ഫാ. എം. തോമസുകുട്ടി, ഫാ. സ്റ്റീഫൻ വൈരമൺ, ഫാ. ഫിലിപ്പ് മാത്യു, ഫാ. റെജി ലൂക്കോസ്, ഫാ. കെ. കെ. തോമസ്, ഫാ. വർഗ്ഗീസ് കോശി, ഫാ. ജേക്കബ് ജോർജ്, ഫാ. ജേക്കബ് പണിക്കർ, സജീവ് വർഗ്ഗീസ്, ഫാ.വി.ജി കോശി വൈദ്യൻ, ഫാ.ജോസ് എം ദാനിയേൽ, ഫാ.ജോൺ പണിക്കർ കോർ എപ്പിസ്കോപ്പ,ഫാ. മാത്യൂ എബ്രഹാം തലവൂർ എന്നിവർ വികാരിമാരായിരുന്നു. ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ വികാരിയായി ഫാ ബേസിൽ ജെ പണിക്കർ സേവനമനുഷ്ടിക്കുന്നു.

1956 ജൂലൈ മാസം 8ാം തീയതി മലങ്കര ഓർത്തോഡോക്സ് സുറിയാനി സഭയുടെ നിരണം ഭദ്രാസനത്തിൻ്റെ കീഴിൽ സ്ഥാപിതമായ ദേവാലയമാണ് തിരുവൻവണ്ടൂർ സെൻ്റ് ജോർജ്ജ് ഓർത്തഡോക്സ് പള്ളി. നിരണം ഭദ്രാസനത്തിൻ്റെ മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്ത ആയിരുന്ന അഭിവന്ദ്യ തോമാ മാർ ദിവന്യാസിയോസ് മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്തായുടെയും, തോട്ടത്തിൽ വീട്ടിൽ ഗീവർഗീസ് അച്ചൻ്റെയും, മറ്റ്‌ വിശ്വാസികളുടെയും പ്രയത്‌നഭലമായി രൂപം കൊണ്ട ദേവാലയമാണ് കൊച്ചുപള്ളി എന്ന് അറിയപ്പെടുന്ന ഈ ദേവാലയം.

ഇതര ക്രിസ്തീയ സഭകളിൽ നിന്നുള്ള സാമ്പത്തിക സഹായ വാഗ്ദാനം മൂലം ഉമയാറ്റുകര സെൻ്റ് തോമസ് പള്ളിയിൽ ഇടവകാംഗങ്ങളായ തിരുവൻവണ്ടൂരിലെ ഭൂരിപക്ഷം ജനങ്ങളും തങ്ങളുടെ ഓർത്തഡോക്സ്‌ വിശ്വാസം ഉപേക്ഷിച്ച് മറ്റ് സഭാവിശ്വാസം സ്വീകരിക്കുന്നതിനിടയായി. ഇതുമൂലം ഉണ്ടായ വിശ്വാസികളുടെ കൊഴിഞ്ഞുപോക്ക്, ഒരു പുതിയ ദേവാലയം പണിയുവാൻ അഭിവന്ദ്യ തോമാ മാർ ദിവന്യാസിയോസ് മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്തക്കും, ഗീവർഗീസ് അച്ചനും പ്രേരണയായി.

ഓർത്തഡോക്സ് വിശ്വാസം ത്യജിക്കാതെ നിലനിന്നിരുന്ന വിശ്വാസികൾക്ക് ആശ്വാസദായകമയി അവർക്കായി ഒരു ചെറിയ പള്ളി പണിയുവാനുള്ള സ്ഥലം വാങ്ങുകയും, അതിൽ ഓലമേഞ്ഞ ഷെഡ് കെട്ടി 1956 ജൂലൈ മാസം 8-ാം തീയതി പ്രഥമബലി അർപ്പിക്കുകയും ചെയ്തു. തിരുമേനിയുടെ കല്പനപ്രകാരം 1957 ജൂലൈ 11 മുതൽ ബഹു. തോട്ടത്തിൽ വീട്ടിൽ ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ് അച്ചനെ വികാരിയായി നിയമിച്ചു. ഉമയാറ്റുകര പള്ളിയുടെ ചാപ്പലായി വി. ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ് സഹദായുടെ നാമത്തിൽ ഈ ചെറിയ ദേവാലയം തിരുമേനിയുടെ കല്പനയാൽ പ്രഖ്യാപിച്ചു.

തോട്ടത്തിൽ വീട്ടിൽ ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ് അച്ചൻ്റെ കാലശേഷം അദ്ദേഹത്തിൻ്റെ മകനായ റ്റി. ജി. സഖറിയ അച്ചൻ 1971 മുതൽ സഹവികാരിയും, പിന്നീട് വികാരിയുമായി ഭരണം നിർവഹിക്കുകയും, ഇടവകയ്ക് സ്വന്തമായി ഒരു ഇടവക കല്ലറപണിയിക്കുകയും, പള്ളി വിപുലീകരിക്കുകയും, മാസത്തിൽ എല്ലാ ഞായറാഴ്ചയും വി. കുർബാനയുള്ള സ്വതന്ത്ര ഇടവകയാക്കുകയും ചെയ്തു. 1993 വരെ അച്ചൻ ഈ ഇടവകയിൽ സ്തുത്യാർഹമായ സേവനമനുഷ്ഠിച്ചു. തുടർന്നുവന്ന വൈദീകരുടെയും, ഇടവക ജനങ്ങളുടെയും പ്രവർത്തനഭലമായി ഇടവക പുരോഗമന വീഥിയിൽ കൂടി നാളിതുവരെ ദൈവകൃപയാൽ കടന്നുപോയി. കൊച്ചുപള്ളി എന്ന് അറിയപ്പെടുന്ന ഈ ദേവാലയം ഇന്ന് തിരുവൻവണ്ടൂറിലെ ജനങ്ങൾക് ഒരു ആശ്രയ കേന്ദ്രമാണ്.

ഓർത്തഡോക്സ്‌ വൈദീക സെമിനാരിയിലെ സീനിയർ അദ്യാപകനായ റവ. ഫാ. ഡോ. നൈനാൻ കെ. ജോർജ്ജ് 2019 മുതൽ ഈ ഇടവകയിൽ വികാരിയായി സേവനം അനുഷ്ഠിച്ചുവരുന്നു. നടപ്പുസാമ്പത്തിക വർഷം ഇടവക ട്രസ്റ്റിയായി ലിജു ഏബ്രഹാം സേവനം അനുഷ്ഠിക്കുന്നു.

n: Thiruvalla-Paliakkara St. George Orthodox Church

n: Puthencruz St. Peter's and St. Paul's Orthodox Church

Established in 1816 this church is a stronghold of Malankara Orthodox Christians in Puthencruz. One of the main families that supports this parish is the Maliakal Kanneth Family.

The church was established by the members of the Kolenchery Church residing in the area. Initially a cross made of wood was established here when the 'raza' (church procession) during the festival of Kolenchery church reached here, marking the beginning of a church here. This cross was called 'Puthen Kurisu' (New Cross). Later a church was consecrated in the place where the Cross was established and regular services began. Subsequently the village itself came to be known by the same name, 'Puthencruz'.

In late 19th century the sacred relics of Mor Kuriakose Sahdo was interred in this church by St. Gregorios of Parumala, presented to Malankara by Antioch. In 1964, reconstruction of the old church building began under the able leadership of the then church vicar Fr. Thomas Cheruvallil (schismatic) and was consecrated on February 15, 1966 by H.H. Moran Mar Baselios Augen I Catholicos of Malankara.

115 families (2022) - In 1939, the Reverend Mulavarikkal Paulose Ramban established the Seenai Monastery at Mambra and a Parish church in the name of St. Kuriakose the Martyr. Our Parish is under the Diocese of Kochi. Today, 130 devoted members actively participate in various spiritual movements, which include those within this parish, continuing to grow in the divine. Despite this, the community remained loyal and defended the seminary and its rights. Considering these circumstances, the diocesan Metropolitan's 1979-80 orders formally designated the Seminary Chapel for parish use, appointing Rev. Father Joseph Areeckal as the first vicar, allowing the seminary and parish to function peacefully together.

ട്രസ്റ്റിമാർ തΩിലുള്ള ഭിന്നതയിലാരം ഭിച്ച്‌ പ. വട്ടശ്ശേരിൽ മാർ ദീവന്നാസേ്യാസിനെ അബ്‌ദുള്ള ബാവാ മുടക്കിയതോടെ ആവിർഭവിച്ച ഭിന്നത പാലൂർ-ചാട്ടുകുളങ്ങര എന്ന്‌ പുരാതന നാമമുള്ള ആർത്താറ്റ്‌ ഇടവകയിലും പ്രകടമായി. തീരെ ന്യൂനപക്ഷമായതിനാൽ ആ പുരാതനപള്ളിയ്‌ക്കു സമീപം 12 പേരുടെ പേരിൽ അന്തേ്യാഖ്യാസിംഹാസനത്തിന്‌ വേണ്ടി ഒരു സമാന്തര ദേവാലയം പണിയാൻ …ീബാ മാർ ഒസ്‌താത്തിയോസ്‌ നേതൃത്വം നൽകി. 1920 ഒക്‌ടോ. 9 ന്‌ ശിലാസ്ഥാപനം നടത്തി. 1930 മാർച്ച്‌ 19 ന്‌ മാർ ഒസ്‌താത്തിയോസ്‌ കാലം ചെയ്യുന്നതുവരെയും ഇവിടെ താമസിച്ചു ഇവിടെത്തന്നെ കബറടങ്ങി. ഒസ്‌താത്തിയോസിന്‌ ശേഷം മാർ യൂലിയോസ്‌ ചുമതല വഹിച്ചു. 1958-ൽ സഭാഐക്യത്തോടെ പള്ളി കൊച്ചി ഭദ്രാസനത്തിൽ ലയിച്ചു. ഇതിൽ അതൃപ്‌തരായി ഒരു ഗ്രൂപ്പ്‌ വ്യവഹാരം ആരംഭിച്ചത്‌ നിലനില്‌ക്കുന്നു. 1962 മാർച്ച്‌ 17-ന്‌ പൗലൂസ്‌ മാർ സേവേറിയോസ്‌ ഇവിടെ വച്ച്‌ കാലം ചെയ്‌തു 18 ന്‌ ഇവിടെതന്നെ കബറടങ്ങി. ആദ്യകബർ വടക്കുഭാഗത്തും രണ്ടാമത്തെ കബർ തെക്കുഭാഗത്തും പള്ളിയകത്ത്‌ സ്ഥിതിചെയ്യുന്നു.

ds: കേളകം സെന്റ്‌ ജോര്‍ജ്ജ് ഓര്‍ത്തഡോക്‍സ്‌ വലിയപള്ളി,പരിശുദ്ധ ഗീവര്‍ഗീസ്‌ സഹദായുടെ നാമത്തില്‍ സ്ഥാപിക്കപ്പെട്ട ഉത്തരമലബാറിലെ ആദ്യദേവാലയം.1955ല്‍ പള്ളി സ്ഥാപിക്കപ്പെട്ടു .1956 september 20 നു ബഹുമാനപ്പെട്ട ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ അച്ചന്‍(വല്യച്ചന്‍) ഇടവകയുടെ വികാരിയായി,50 വര്‍ഷത്തില്‍ അധികം ഇടവകയെ നയിച്ചു.ഇപ്പോള്‍ വികാരിയായി Fr.Samson.M.Simon സേവനം അനുഷ്ടിക്കുന്നു.180 ല്‍ പരം കുടുംബങ്ങള്‍ ഇന്ന് ഇടവകയില്‍ ഉണ്ട്.മലങ്കരസഭയുടെ അഭിമാനമായ ഈ പള്ളി ഉത്തരമലബാറില്‍ ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ സഹദായുടെ നാമത്തില്‍ വിളക്ക്നേര്‍ച്ച ഉള്ള ഏക ദേവാലയമാണ്.എല്ലമാസത്തെയും അവസാനത്തെ വെള്ളിയാഴ്ച വിളക്ക്നേര്‍ച്ച നടക്കുന്നു.മലങ്കര സഭയുടെ എല്ലാ തലത്തിലും ശ്രദ്ധിക്കപ്പെടുന്ന നേട്ടങ്ങളും സേവനങ്ങളും കാഴ്ചവെക്കുന്ന ഇടവകയെ പ.കാതോലിക്കാബാവ 2010ല്‍ വലിയപള്ളിയായി ഉയര്‍ത്തി.ഇടവക അംഗമായ ശ്രി .പൈലി വാത്യട്ടു സഭാ മാനേജിംഗ് കമ്മിറ്റി മെംബര്‍ ആണ്.മലങ്കര സഭയുടെ ബത്തേരി ഭദ്രാസനത്തിലെ പ്രധാന ദേവാലയങ്ങളില്‍ ഒന്നാണ് ഈ പള്ളി.നമ്മെ വിട്ട്പിരിഞ്ഞ ഇടവകയുടെ ശില്പിയും നമ്മുടെ ആത്മീയ ഗുരുവും ആയിരുന്ന വല്യച്ചന്റെ സ്നേഹനിര്‍ഭരമായ ഓര്‍മ്മയില്‍,പ്രാര്‍ത്ഥനയോടെ എല്ലാ ഇടവക അംഗങ്ങളെയും ഈ ഗ്രൂപ്പിലേക്ക് സ്വാഗതം ചെയുന്നു.

ds: The Deolali St. Mary's Orthodox Church which was initially formed as a congregation in 1953 was merged with Nashik St. George Orthodox Church on 2nd September 2017 due to a lack of members. The parish still exists with representation in the Malankara Association however.

n: Khopoli St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church
ds: Khopoli Orthodox Congregation was started by Rev Fr K I Philip Ramban. Prayer meetings and services were being conducted since 1990’s. For the last 13 years the services are being conducted on regular basis. In 2011 the congregation was declared as an independent parish. Now services are being conducted every second Sunday of the month at St. Antony’s Catholic Church. Prayer meetings are being conducted on every Sunday. Very Rev Fr George Modiyll Cor Episcopa, Rev Fr C J Joshua, Rev Fr Thomas Chacko, Rev Fr Joshy P Jacob, Rev Fr Abraham Joseph served the parish. Rev Fr. Geevarghese Chacko (Anish) is serving as the present Vicar.

n: Lonavala St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church
ds: The orthodox church activities for lonavla was started in the year 1958 by late mr t.V koruthu. He was elected as a member of the managing committee of kirkee/pune orthodox syrian church in 1960. Holy qurbana was celebrated at lonavla on holidays, 26th january & 15th august and also on the 5th sunday of the month . The vicar of kirkee/pune used to come to lonavla for conducting the service. Sunday prayer meetings started on a regular basis from the year 1971. Since 1958 till today we conduct the holy qurbana at “all saints church” (csi) barabunglow lonavala on rent. Under the guidance of rev fr p.V kuriakose we formed mgm prayer group at lonavla in the year 1977. A plot of land about 4500 sq ft was purchased for building a church on 06/12/1987 in the joint names of four members, t.V kunjumen,alexander koruthu,k.J.George and koshy varghese . Foundation stone for building a small church was laid by late lamented his grace phillipose mar theophilus on 26.04.1990. There were only fifteen members at that time and due to insufficient funds the project could not be completed. The land was transferred in the name of metropolitan of bombay, his grace geevarghese mar coorilos on 07.04.2000. Since 1988 holy qurbana is offered once in a month at lonavala. Presently rev fr john mathai is our vicar. The lonavala parshiners attend the services like christmas,holy week, easter, pentecost and other feast days in dehuroad/ chinchwad/kirkee/pune church. Even though lonavla being such a small congregation of only nine family members, his grace geevarghese mar coorilos has celebrated the holy qurbana several times at lonavala, we are very thankful to our beloved thirumeni.

n: Nerul St. Mary's Malankara Orthodox Church
ds: ST MARY’S ORTHODOX SYRIAN CHURCH, NERUL Since 1985, Orthodox believers of Nerul node were attending the Holy Mass at St. Thomas Aramana Chruch, Vashi and prayer meetings had been going on at member’s residences on Sundays at Nerul, led by Rev Fr Thomas Varghese and Rev Fr T U Thomas. With the expansion of the township and a surge in Orthodox believers, St Mary’s Congregation came into existence. In 2004 it was declared as a parish. Holy Qurbana were conducted twice a month. Initially it started with 49 members. At present there are 111 members on the roll. From 2004 onwards there are regular services. Rev Fr T E Issac, Rev Fr Joji George, Rev Fr Abraham Joseph, Rev Fr M E Joseph & Rev Fr Thomas Mathai served as vicars. During this period, Sunday services were conducted at different places like CIDCO Community hall, Nerul, Meridian Apartments, Sector 6-Nerul, St Augustine’s High School, Sector11-Nerul, Municipal High School, Sector 4-Nerul and Municipal High School, Sector 20-Nerul. On 16th March 2011, the church members with the combined efforts of Rev Fr M E Joseph and managing committee formed a trust names “St Mary’s Orthodox Trust” and registered with the charity commissioner, Thane. This is in fact a great achievement. Subsequently, in 2012, with the co-operation and effort of members, a 3 BHK flat was purchased at sector 27, Nerul (E). Spiritual organizations like Sunday School, MGOCSM, OCYM, MMVS and Cottage prayer meetings are functioning regularly. Rev Fr K P Varghese is the present Vicar.

n: Roha St. Peter's and St. Paul's Malankara Orthodox Church
ds: History of St. Peter's and St. Paul's Orthodox Church, Roha This parish was formed as a congregation on 1995 June 19, through a Kalpana for one Holy Qurbana every month. H. G. Geevarghese Mar Coorilos celebrated Holy Qurbana at J.M. Rathi School twice and declared as a Parish in 1995 through a Kalpana dated 27.08.1995. Since 1985, weekly prayer meetings were held on Sundays at the residences of our members. Rev. Fr. Lazarus OIC and Rev. Fr. P.A. Kuriakose conducted occasionally Holy Qurbana at the residence of a member between 1989 and 1995. Thereafter, Holy Qurbana was held at Rathi School and Catholic Church. In April 1996, ten cents of land was purchased for building a church at Roha. After the establishment of Gregorian Community, Holy Qurbana is conducted at the Chapel at Aarey Budruk and later on at Killa in Roha. After declaring as a Parish in 1995, Rev. Fr. Abraham Joseph, Rev. Fr. T.U. Thomas, Rev. Fr. Thomas Varghese, Rev. Fr. Thomas K. Chacko, Rev. Fr. Joshy P. Jacob, Rev. Fr. B.M. Thomas and Rev. Fr. Sam Oommen Panackamattom were served as Vicars of the church. Rev. Fr. Alin Joseph Alex is the present Vicar.

n: Tughlaqabad St. Thomas Palatial Chapel
ds: By 1985, the Diocesan headquarters moved to its own building, the Delhi Orthodox Centre in Tughlaqabad in South Delhi. An architecturally distinctive three-storey building, the centre was dedicated by Catholicos Baselios Mar Thoma Mathews I and inaugurated by the Vice-President of India, R Venkataraman, in November 1984. With the St. Thomas Chapel in the middle, the centre is the residence of the Metropolitan and houses, besides the secretariat of the Diocesan Council, a library, a publication unit, the People's Education Society, Sophia Society, Sarva Dharma Nilaya, Dhyan Mandir and Niti Santi Kendra, engaged in a variety of complementary activities. In 1991, the Diocese was strengthened by the arrival of Job Mar Philoxenos as the Assistant Metropolitan.

n: Indore St. Mary's Malankara Orthodox Church
ds: This church holds the designation of being the first church in India where the Coptic liturgy was celebrated (on October 29 2016).

n: Makarpura-Jambuva St. George Malankara Orthodox Chapel
ds: An independent chapel. Formerly organized as Makarpura Congregation.

n: Mhow St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church
ds: Church is located in the compound of MGM English Medium School, Kalibillod which is also run by the church

n: Sana'a St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Parish currently inactive due to war and Jihadists destroying churches and martyring the faithful in Yemen. The parish had its own church. Many times the faithful also prayed at the Catholic Church in Sanaa at P.O. Box 16050, Hadha, Sana’a.

n: Gold Coast St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Gold Coast: Our first *Holy Qurbana* for the newly formed *St. Gregorios Malankara (Indian) Orthodox Church centred on Gold Coast in the name of St. Gregorios [Parumala Thirumeni] will be held on Tuesday, September 20, 2022, at 6:00 p.m.

n: Kuala Lumpur St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Cathedral (Brickfields)
ds:
200 families (2018) - There are 630 Malankara Orthodox laity in Malaysia and 2 priests serving across 6 congregations under this parish.

The first parish that the Malankara Orthodox Church had outside India was Malaya-Singapore. These two places, under British colonial rule, had many tea, coffee and rubber estates. Most
of the labourers in those estates were Tamils and Chinese. A large number of Christians from Kerala were also employed as the overseers and office staff. Most of these people were from Central Travancore and majority of them were Marthomites (largest minority was Orthodox). They had six or seven churches and one school there. The Orthodox had one church each in Malaya and Singapore. There was a joint
council for these two churches which worked hard to see that the vicars could easily carry out their responsibilities.

Originally the priest would come via ship from Madras to Singapore to Penang to Kuala Lumpur serving the congregations in the three cities.

Parish of H. G. Abraham Mar Epiphanios Metropolitan, first Malankara Orthodox bishop born outside India.

n: Hartford St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
We are the Connecticut parish of the North East American Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. Growing since 2010, ours is a community united by a mix of young hearted faithful-orthodoxy and fun-fellowship. We are located in Newington, a central location to the entire State of Connecticut.

Our Vicar, Rev. Fr. Kuriakose (Alex) Abraham leads our congregation in Sunday Mass and prayers. Our faithful also gets to congregate during Prayer meetings held once a month on Saturdays.

n: Washington D.C. St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Founded in September 1965 under the leadership of the late Rev. K. C. Thomas, later H.G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios, this parish in the Greater Washington, D.C. area is among the earliest Malankara Orthodox congregations in North America and was the first organized Indian Christian congregation in the region. Established by young immigrants from Kerala, it served the Washington, Maryland, and Northern Virginia communities. The parish acquired 1.2 acres of land in 2001, with the groundbreaking performed by H.H. Baselios Mar Thoma Didymos I in 2006. The present church was consecrated by H.G. Mathews Mar Barnabas in November 2008, following construction initiated by Rev. Fr. Dr. P. C. Thomas and completed under Rev. Fr. Santhosh Joshua.

n: New York Holy Cross Indian-American Orthodox Mission Church (Manhattan)
ds: Lampman Chapel in Union Theological Seminary 3041 Broadway at 121st Street New York, NY 10027

n: White Plains St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
Saint Mary’s Malankara Orthodox Church, White Plains, New York is a parish under the jurisdiction of the Northeast American Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. For over a decade this parish has been worshiping at 99 Park Avenue, White Plains, New York.

This building, known as the Malankara Jacobite Center is not owned by the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, nor is owned by the Syriac Orthodox Church. Rather, it is under a private incorporation which has been leasing the building to Rev. Fr. Paulose T. Peter, the Vicar of St. Mary's Orthodox Syrian Church and our parish has been using the building through that lease.

In October 2022, the organization informed Rev. Fr. Paulose T. Peter that the lease will not be renewed. Our parish continues to be an integral part of the Northeast American Diocese and has already started worshiping in an alternate facility from October 9, 2022, onwards.

n: Beasley Holy Apostles Palatial Chapel
ds: Holy Qurbana to be conducted at Urshlem Aramana Chapel, Beasley every Saturday Morning. Morning Prayer will start at 9.00 AM followed by the Holy Qurbana.

n: Bellwood St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Cathedral
ds: 72 families (2000) - Organized in 1994 under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Daniel George following a split from the St. Gregorios Orthodox parish in Elmhurst, this congregation celebrated its first Holy Divine Liturgy on May 22, 1994, led by His Grace Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios, Senior Metropolitan of the Malankara Orthodox Church in America. Early services were held at St. Cyprian's Episcopal Church in Chicago as the parish grew from 20 to more than 72 families. The congregation purchased its Bellwood church building in 2000, where it was consecrated that October by Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios on the Memorial Day of St. Gregorios of Parumala. In 2003, the parish was elevated to cathedral status, becoming the second Malankara Orthodox cathedral in the United States. Rev. Fr. Ham Joseph serves as vicar.

n: Carrollton St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Popularly known as the Church of India, informally as "COI".

n: Chicago St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: 75 families (2023) - Founded in 1971, this was the first Malankara Orthodox parish established in Chicago, with Rev. Fr. Kurian Thottupuram initially celebrating the liturgy at the Convent Chapel of St. Mary of the Lake before services moved to St. Peter’s Episcopal Church in 1972. The parish received official recognition from H.G. Mathews Mar Athanasius in 1973 and was incorporated in Illinois in 1976. Very Rev. Dr. Kurian Thottupuram Cor Episcopa served as founding vicar until 1980, followed by Very Rev. Dr. M. E. Idiculla Cor Episcopa and later Very Rev. Koshy V. Poovathur, under whose leadership the first permanent property at 3735 N. Narragansett was purchased and consecrated in 1990 by H.G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios. The congregation later acquired its current property at 6099 N. Northcott Ave in 2016 under Rev. Fr. Ham Joseph, with the consecration conducted by H.H. Moran Mar Baselios Marthoma Paulose II. Since 2023, Rev. Fr. Shinto T. David has served as vicar. The parish includes more than 75 families, with third-generation members actively participating, while pioneer Rev. Deacon George Poovathur serves on the Managing Committee of the Malankara Orthodox Church.

n: Denver St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: 20 families - Established in Lakewood, Colorado, this parish was built in 2006 to serve the spiritual needs of the Malankara Orthodox faithful in the area. The church community consists of approximately 20 families who gather together in faith, worship, and fellowship.

n: Hollywood St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: In 1983, the church was established. It was the first Indian church in Florida.

n: Kansas City St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church
ds: 20 families - The origins of this parish trace back to 2002, when Orthodox faithful in the Kansas City area gathered after Mr. Abraham Mathew connected with Rev. Fr. Mathew Zachariah of Denver. The first Holy Qurbana was celebrated on November 16, 2002. With continued support from visiting priests, including Rev. Fr. Chacko V. Isaac and Rev. Fr. Cherian (Sunny) M. Kunnel, the congregation was formed and named St. Gregorios in 2008. It was officially recognized as a congregation under the Diocese of Southwest America on September 9, 2009, and elevated to a parish on November 2, 2011, with Rev. Fr. Diju (Zachariah) Skariah as its first resident Vicar. In 2015, the parish purchased a 2.63-acre property with a 4,000+ square foot church building. Today, the parish serves approximately 20 families in the Kansas City area.

n: Oak Lawn St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Established in 1982, this Malankara Orthodox parish began in Chicago as a small extension of the city's first Orthodox congregation under the leadership of its founding vicar, Very Rev. Kuriakos Thottupuram Cor-Episcopos. Rev. Fr. Cherian Kunnel later assisted the parish before serving a congregation in Oklahoma City, while Rev. Fr. Sunoj Malayil Oommen was assistant vicar from 2005 to 2010. Since June 2010, Rev. Fr. Abi Chacko has served as the parish's second vicar. The congregation relocated to Park Ridge in 2001, where its campus includes a church sanctuary, Sunday School building, and attached parsonage. Among Malankara Orthodox parishes in the Chicago area, it is one of the smallest congregations. The sanctuary features extensive Orthodox iconography, including shrines dedicated to St. Mary, St. Thomas, St. Jude Thaddeus, St. Gregorios of Parumala, St. George, the Transfiguration, and a large icon depicting the life of St. Mary flanked by Archangels Michael and Gabriel.

n: Phoenix St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
The worship service of the Indian Orthodox Church was introduced to the Valley of the Sun in the early 1990’s, as part of an Ecumenical Community. The first Divine Liturgy (Holy Qurbana) was celebrated in August 1995 by Rev. Fr. Yohannan Panicker at a private facility of a parishioner. Then after, the Holy Qurbana was celebrated at a rented facility, which coincidentally turned out to be the same facility the parish owns today at 2137 E. Yale St., Phoenix, AZ – 85006. This venue was rented out for about eight months, back then, and later the venue was changed to Gethsemane Lutheran Church, Tempe, AZ. Rev. Fr. Yohannan Panicker served the community once a month until March of 1998. Yohannan Panicker Achen was later substituted with Rev. Fr. Sabu Thomas until June of 2003.

From July 2003, Rev. Fr. Philip Abraham, the Vicar of St. Mary’s Orthodox Church, Los Angeles, had graciously agreed to serve on a monthly basis. Rev. Fr. Joseph Kalapurackal also served the community for a short period in 2005 as a resident priest.

As more and more Indian Orthodox families moved to Phoenix and adjoining sub-urban areas, the need for establishing a Malankara Orthodox Church community was ever more pertinent. A formal request regarding this was communicated to the American Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Church.

On January 11, 2006, a Kalpana was issued by Late and Lamented H. G. Mathews Mar Barnabas, Metropolitan and H. G. Zachariah Mar Nicolovos, Assistant Metropolitan of the then undivided American Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Church, recognizing the community as St. Thomas Orthodox Congregation of India. Rev. Fr. Philip Abraham (Roi Achen) was appointed as the Vicar and President of the congregation. Worship was held twice every month from 2006 until July of 2009. Roi Achen served the spiritual needs of the community until October 11, 2008. As one of the founding fathers of the community, he served as the Vicar and President since its establishment. He was instrumental in leading and developing this infant community.

On October 12, 2008, Rev. Fr. Slomo Isac George was appointed as the new Vicar and President of our congregation. The community was overjoyed to have a much needed resident Priest to lead the community.

Since there was a resident Vicar available, everyone had the urge for worship to be held on all Sundays and to celebrate all the feasts and sacraments. Holy Qurbana was celebrated on Saturdays at rented facilities. From July of 2009 until September of 2015, worship was held at the Knight of Pythias center in Tempe, AZ. The South-West American Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Church was formed in June 2008 and our parish became a part of the newly formed diocese, under the guidance and leadership of H. G. Alexios Mar Eusebius. We had the honor of welcoming H.G. in July 2009 for the first time in Phoenix. On July 5, 2009, His Grace verbally elevated the congregation to the level of a parish after the Holy Qurbana. St. Thomas Congregation of Phoenix was officially elevated as St. Thomas Orthodox Church of India on August 03, 2009, with the declaration kalpana from H.G. Alexios Mar Eusebius.

With the hard work and dedication of the Vicar, Fr. Slomo George and the parishioners, the dream of having our own facility came true. Many people were very instrumental for the purchase and renovation of the church building and surrounding property.

On September 18th, 2015, the Diocesan Metropolitan H. G. Alexios Mar Eusebius consecrated the newly renovated church with the presence of Priests and Deacons of the diocese.

On May 15, 2016, Rev. Fr. Slomo George was relieved from his duties. Achen and his family worked tirelessly to build the community in Phoenix and achieve the goal of owning a facility.

Rev. Fr. George T. David (Shinto) was appointed as the new Vicar & President on May 20, 2016. From September of 2016, Achen and family moved to Phoenix as a resident priest. The current priest is Fr. Emmanuel Punnoose (Atlanta).

n: Pompano Beach St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: In November 1983, The FIRST Holy Eucharist according to Syrian Orthodox tradition was conducted by Rev. Fr. M. T. Kurian in South Florida. On Sunday December 18, 1983, after Holy Eucharist Service by the visiting priest Rev. Fr. Joy Pyngolil, a few members met at the house of Mr. Mohan Mathen to discuss the formation of a congregation and prayer meeting. Thus, the St. Thomas Malankara Orthodox Congregation was formed. American Diocesan Metropolitan His Grace Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios appointed Rev. Fr. Johnny George as the First Vicar of St. Thomas Malankara Orthodox Church of India, South Florida. Subsequently, Rev. Fr. Yesudasan Pappan, Rev. Fr. Daniel Pulleli, Rev. Fr. George John,Rev. Fr. P. M. Zachariah, Rev. Fr. George Daniel, Rev. Fr. Johnson Pappachan and Rev. Fr. Joseph Kalapurayil were appointed as the vicars of this parish by the Diocesan Metropolitans. With the grace of God, the guidance of Vicar Rev. Fr. Joseph Kalapurayil, unceasing prayers and financial support of all members, we are blessed with a beautiful permanent worship facility in Pompano Beach.

n: San Diego St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Chapel
ds: The venue is St. Bartholomew's Episcopal Church, 16275 Pomerado Rd, Poway at St. Bartholomew's Episcopal Church in the Chapel Room.

n: Seattle St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: 70 families - St. Thomas Malankara Orthodox Church, Renton, Washington, began in 1986 as a prayer fellowship of four Orthodox believers. The parish celebrated its first Holy Qurbana in 1988, led by Rev. Fr. Michael Hatcher, Rev. Fr. James Pike, and Deacon Gabriel Pike. Under the guidance of H.G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios and other visiting hierarchs, the congregation grew steadily, establishing a church building fund in 1991. Rev. Fr. James Pike was appointed Vicar in 1996, and the parish was incorporated in Washington State in 1997. By God's grace, the church's permanent sanctuary was consecrated on May 27, 2011, by H.G. Alexios Mar Eusebius, serving the faithful in the Pacific Northwest ever since.

n: South Florida St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
St. Gregorios Orthodox Church of India, South Florida, started as a small congregation in August 2000. With the approval of H.G. Mathews Mar Barnabas, Fr. George John served as the officiating priest. Services were conducted at St. Nicholas Orthodox Church, Fort Lauderdale since the beginning. Very Rev. Fr. Kirrill Gvosdev, vicar of St. Nicholas Orthodox Church, was very kind to provide their church and its facilities for our worship. On December 30, 2000, H. G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios, senior Metropolitan of the American Diocese, offered Holy Qurbana here, and in December 2000 H. G. Mathews Mar Barnabas, Metropolitan of the American Diocese, declared the congregation as a parish in the American Diocese in the name St. Gregorios Orthodox church of India, South Florida and appointed Fr. George John as the vicar.

The members of the parish took much enthusiasm in attending the Sunday service even though it was conducted very early in the morning at 6:00 am. After the service the parking lot and people’s vehicles was used to conduct Sunday Schools. The parishners also conducted refreshments and the meetings of the church at the parking lot.

In February 2009, by the grace of God, the church bought a building that belonged to a Ukrainian club in Hollywood. The city granted the Certificate of Use as a church in June 2009, and the renovation work on the building was completed by October 2010. Fr. George John performed the temporary consecration on November 6th and offered Holy Qurbana & conducted the feast of Parumala Thirumeni on November 7th. The official consecration will be done by H. G. Alxios Mar Eusebius, Metropolitan of the Diocese of South West America, on January14th and 15th.

n: Spokane St. Gregorios American-Malankara Orthodox Church
ds:
70 families - Established in Spokane, Washington, in 1987, this parish traces its origins to an Orthodox prayer community formed in 1984 under the leadership of Fr. Michael Hatcher and Gita Hatcher. Originally a small gathering of about 30 people, the parish grew into a vibrant multicultural Orthodox community serving Indian, Ethiopian, Eritrean, Middle Eastern, and other faithful. After worshiping in several rented locations, the congregation moved to its current facility in 2017. Over 35 years of ministry, Fr. Michael and the parish have emphasized English-based liturgy, outreach, and service to the surrounding community. The parish also gave rise to St. Mary’s Ethiopian Orthodox Church through its ministry among Ethiopian and Eritrean believers.

Notable members of parish: Fr. Anthony Creech

n: Stafford St. Ephrem Indian Orthodox Chapel
ds: A very great moderate chapel to accommodate 100 people. It is designed in such a way that you are really visiting a Byzantine-styled church. Very calming and peaceful atmosphere. First time experience to see the Icon painting of St. Gregorios of Parumala, St. Vattaseril Thirumeni (Patron saints of India) and Archangel Michael.

n: Chicago Malankara Orthodox Christian Society Centre
ds: The Malankara Orthodox Christian Society of Chicago (MOCS) is a non-profit organization established to provide a unified forum for Malayalee Orthodox Christians in the Chicago area to preserve their spiritual, cultural, and community traditions. Centered on Christ, MOCS promotes fellowship, prayer, worship, and opportunities for families, youth, and children to grow together in faith. The society hosts various community events, including Family Nights and cultural celebrations such as the MOCS Carnival. MOCS was formally inaugurated during its Family Night event on May 10, 2025, marking a new initiative to strengthen unity and fellowship among Orthodox Christians in the Chicagoland community.

n: Elmhurst St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church
ds: 230 families (2025) - Established in February 1978, this parish began in Evanston, Illinois, with approximately 30 families gathering under the leadership of its first Vicar, Fr. Geevarghese Aroopala Cor-Episcopa, in the name of St. Gregorios of Parumala. The congregation moved to Oak Park in 1984 and grew to become the largest Malankara Orthodox parish in the Chicagoland area, giving rise to daughter parishes including St. Gregorios Orthodox Cathedral, Bellwood, and St. Gregorios Jacobite Church, Oak Park, along with a Qurbana center in Elgin. Under Fr. Dr. M.K. Thomas, appointed Vicar in 1993 by H.G. Mathews Mar Barnabas, the parish experienced significant spiritual growth. In 2010, Rev. Fr. Ninan V. George became Vicar, guiding the parish into its current home in Elmhurst.

n: Calgary St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds: 120 families (2026) - Established as a parish on December 21, 2002 (St. Thomas Day), this Calgary congregation began as a prayer group of Malankara Orthodox faithful and other Malayalee Christians, with occasional Holy Eucharistic services by visiting priests and bishops. Initially consisting of about 10 families, the parish has grown to over 100 families. It was placed under the Diocese of Canada on November 1, 2004, under H.G. Dr. Zachariah Mar Nicholovos. The parish purchased land in 2015, received construction approval in 2024, and the foundation stone was laid by H.G. Thomas Mar Ivanios on June 29, 2024. The church building was consecrated on May 29–30, 2026, blessed by H.H. Moran Mar Baselios Marthoma Mathews III.

n: Vancouver St. George Indian Orthodox Church (Surrey)
ds: 80 families (2026), 50 families (2024), 35 families (2022) - St. George Malankara Orthodox Church, Vancouver, British Columbia, traces its origins to Orthodox prayer gatherings among fewer than 40 Malayalee families in the early 1990s. Following H.G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios' visit in 1997, regular Holy Qurbana began in 2003 through the dedicated ministry of Rev. Ramban Lazarus, followed by Rev. Fr. Daniel Chacko and Rev. Fr. T. U. Jacob, under whose leadership the parish was officially established and registered in 2007. Rev. Fr. P. C. George's tenure beginning in 2010 revitalized parish life and launched the church building initiative. In 2024, under H.G. Thomas Mar Ivanios, the parish was designated the "Parumala of Canada" in recognition of its custody of the relics of St. Gregorios of Parumala, a historic distinction within the Malankara Orthodox Church in Canada.

n: Edmonton St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Founded through home gatherings in 1972, this parish began with 13 Malayali families who came together for worship in Edmonton. The first Holy Qurbana was celebrated by Rev. Fr. A. K. Cherian, who traveled from New York, with families also joining from Calgary, Fort McMurray, High Prairie, Hinton, Westlock, and Saskatoon. In 1976, the congregation was formally established as St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church and approved by the Holy See. The parish was incorporated in 1982 under the Alberta Religious Societies Act and received its first resident Vicar, Rev. Fr. George John, in 1986. After 13 years of worshiping in borrowed sanctuaries, the parish purchased its own building in 1987, consecrated in 1988 by H.G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios. The parish joined the Diocese of Southwest America in 2009, installed the relics of St. Gregorios of Parumala in 2024, and purchased 30 acres of land in November 2024.

n: Aberdeen St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Established in May 2009, the Indian Orthodox Parish in Aberdeen held its first Qurbana on the 20th of that month and was later declared a parish by H.G. Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios. Holy Qurbana has been celebrated on the 2nd and 4th Sundays since January 2015.

n: Bielefeld St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church
ds: The Parish traces its informal existence to fellowships that have existed in the region since the late 1970s. Under the initiative taken by the Late Lamented Philipose Mar Theophilos of Bombay and Angamaly Diocese, Fr. Korah Varghese was appointed as the priest-in-charge of the community in Germany in 1972, serving faithfully as Vicar for about 3 decades.

n: Birmingham St. Stephen's Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
The inception of the new millennium marked the beginning of an ever-growing influx of the members of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church across the length and breadth of the United Kingdom, and Birmingham and its surrounding areas were no exception. In early 2002, the seeds for St. Stephen’s Indian Orthodox Church were sown in the form of prayer meetings that were conducted in the Birmingham area. With the support of many brothers and sisters from London and Bristol, the first ever Holy Qurbana in Birmingham was celebrated in November 2003.

By 17th June 2007, the congregation was officially declared as St. Stephen’s Indian Orthodox Church- a parish under the Canada and Europe Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church by the then Diocesan Metropolitan H. G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios of blessed memory. The parish is greatly indebted to the Holy Trinity Church, Sutton Coldfield, St. Francis Hall at the University of Birmingham & The Walker Memorial Hall in Edgbaston for their warmth and generosity in allowing us to use their premises for worship, every 2nd and 4th Sunday, as well as during major feasts and fasts.

The desire to acquire an own place of worship was ever-present in the hearts of each parishioner. By God’s grace, the intercession of St. Stephen, and under the zealous leadership of our Diocesan Metropolitan, Vicars, Trustees, Secretaries, Committee Members, leaders of all spiritual organisation and with sincere prayers of every member of the parish, the current place of worship in Sheldon was purchased in April 2019. The church was consecrated by the then Diocesan Metropolitan, H. G. Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios on 10th & 11th December 2021. Since the Holy Consecration, the parish has been blessed with a substantial growth in the number of new members, and from early 2023, Holy Qurbana is being celebrated every week.

St. Stephen’s Indian Orthodox Church has made major contributions to the growth and development of the Diocese of U.K., Europe and Africa by providing gifted and able leaders to faithfully execute administrative duties, in addition to being elected as leaders of various Spiritual Organisations at the Diocesan Level. At the Parish level, all the major Spiritual Organisations of the Church, such as Sunday School, Martha Mariam Vanitha Samajam (MMVS), Youth Movement, Students’ Movement and AMOSS are functioning fully and bringing spiritual nourishment to all the members, and the local community. The other spiritual wings of the parish are the Prayer Group, Church Choir and Ecumenical Relations.

Under the pastoral care and leadership of our new Diocesan Metropolitan, H. G. Abraham Mar Stephanos, who played an integral part in the establishment of this parish in the early 2000s, the current Vicar, Rev. Fr. Mathew Abraham Palathinkal, and relying on the intercession of St. Stephen, the protomartyr, St. Stephen’s Indian Orthodox Church is gleefully looking to the future with great hope.

n: Bristol St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
In August 2002, a small flock of worshippers start to conduct family gatherings for prayer meetings in the homes of those in Bristol. In October 2002, for the first time, Fr. Abraham Thomas the then Vicar of St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church, London conducted evening prayers and Holy Communion in Bristol. This initiative is pivotal to the history of the commencement of our very own regular evening prayers and Holy Communion service in Bristol.

In April 2003, SMIOC Bristol observed the first holy week. The prayers were performed by Fr. Abraham George in a rented hall. In August 2003 the Late Lamented His Grace Dr Thomas Mar Makarios Metropolitan of the then Diocese of North America and UK, Europe, and Canada made his maiden visit and proclaimed the congregation in Bristol as a parish of Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in the presence of Fr. Abraham Thomas and Fr. Varghese Mathew. His Grace also appointed Rev. Fr Varghese Mathew as the first Vicar of the church.

The services were held initially on every second and fourth Saturday at St Vincent De-Paul Catholic Church until the acquirement of the current church property in 2013. On the 6th and 7th September 2013, the parish was consecrated by the Supreme Head of the Malankara (Indian) Orthodox Syrian Church, His Holiness Moran Mar Baselios Mar Thoma Paulose II, Catholicos and Malankara Metropolitan assisted by Late Lamented His Grace Thomas Mar Athanasios Metropolitan, Diocese of Chengannur and our diocese bishop, His Grace Dr Mathews Mar Thimothios Metropolitan, Diocese of the UK, Europe & Africa.

All spiritual organizations such as Sunday School, MGOCSM (Youth Movement), MOMS and Prayer Group are actively functioning in the parish.

n: Cambridge St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: The St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church, Cambridge is the first Church of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in the Cambridgeshire / East Anglia region. It was founded from the desire in the minds of handful Malankara Orthodox immigrants to this area in early 2005 to congregate and worship Almighty God in the traditions and practices of the Indian Orthodox Church. With the support of Rev. Fr. Abraham Thomas (the Vicar of London St. Gregorios Parish) and the tireless effort of the members in the area, the first Holy Qurbana in Cambridgeshire was conducted on 14th January 2006 with less than ten families at the St. Luke Methodist Church, Papworth Everard, Cambridge. Thereafter, Holy Qurbana has been conducted regularly on the second Saturdays of every month. In June 2007, the late Metropolitan Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios Metropolitan of the then UK-Canada and Europe Diocese elevated this Congregation into an independent Parish with St. Thomas as its patron.

n: City of London St. George Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
The St George's Indian Orthodox Church, London is a church under the UK, Europe, and Africa Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church of India.

The Indian Orthodox church has had a presence in London since the 1970s and used to celebrate Holy Eucharist at St. Andrew-by-the-wardrobe Church near Blackfriars every Sunday. The Indian Orthodox community has been fortunate to continue their service at this church since 1978.

After the parishioners purchased their own church in Brockley, London, the worship at St. Andrew-by-the-wardrobe Church continued under the spiritual guidance of St. Gregorios Church, Brockley and the generosity of the Church of England.

Due to unforeseen circumstances, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the worship at St. Andrew-by-the-wardrobe Church was disrupted for a few months. However, with the help of the Church of England and others, a new place of worship was found at St. Margaret Pattens Church of England, Eastcheap. The Holy Eucharist continues at St Margaret Pattens since 27 November 2022.

During his episcopal visit on 02 October 2022, the then Diocesan Bishop HG. Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios Metropolitan declared this as a new congregation and it was officially named the 'St George's Indian Orthodox Church, City of London'. His Grace also appointed Very Rev. Fr Abraham George Cor-Episcopa as the Vicar.

On the 1st of January 2023, the church began its service as a new congregation with the blessings and benediction of Abraham Mar Stephanos Metropolitan. We are deeply appreciative of the continuous support and guidance from our Diocesan Bishop, H.G Abraham Mar Stephanos Metropolitan.

From its humble beginnings as a small community, our congregation has grown to include 70 families. Every Sunday, we welcome new individuals, including students, to worship with us at our church in the heart of London. It is with great pride and honour that we serve our community in London and carry on the legacy of service that began in the 1970s.

n: Clonmel (Tipperary) St. Kuriakose Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Commenced as a Prayer fellowship in February 2024 in County Tipperary, Republic of Ireland. Recognized as a Congregation on 01 July 2024 by Diocesan Metropolitan HE Abraham Mar Stephanos appointing Fr. Mathew K. Mathew as priest-in-charge. Acquired the historic Franciscan Friary at Carrick-on-Suir on 02 September 2024 – a property covering 4,200 square feet set on a picturesque 1.5-acre site, offering a serene and sacred environment for worship and community activities. Renovation work was completed in October 2024 and the Church was consecrated on 22, 23 November 2024 by Diocesan metropolitan HE Abraham Mar Stephanos and Synod Secretary HE Dr. Yuhanon mar Chrysostomos. Regular Holy Qurbana, Sunday School, Prayer groups, Bible study, and activities for OCYM, MMVS, etc.

n: Colchester St. Stephen's Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
St. Stephens IOC Colchester had its humble beginnings in a prayer meeting held at Well Methodist Church, Colchester, attended by 40 faithful, including Rev. Fr. Liju Varghese and Rev. Fr. Ranju Skariah on 23/10/2022. It was very evident at this initial meeting that there was strong interest in having a Holy Qurbana in Colchester. Accordingly, the first HQ was solemnised by Rev Fr. Liju Varghese, at St Mathew’s Church, Colchester with over 70 attendees on 26/11/2022.

Subsequently, a formal written request signed by 22 families was submitted to the Diocesan Metropolitan, requesting congregation status. Formation of the congregation was approved, and named after St Stephen by His Eminence Abraham Mar Stephanos, effective from 1/1/2023. Rev. Fr Liju Varghese was appointed as the Priest in Charge. Parish status was granted by the diocesan metropolitan on 28/4/2024.

The Parish has since grown in strength, both numerically and spiritually over the last 2.5 years. Currently, Holy Qurbanas are held on the first and third Sundays of every month, in addition to other feast days and special services, like Passion Week and Christmas. Spiritual organisations are functioning actively in their respective areas - AMOSS, Sunday school, OCYM, MMVS and Prayer Meeting Group.

n: Cologne-Bonn St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
In the early 1970s, lured by employment prospects, members of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, began to migrate to Germany. As the members of the community increased in Bonn-Köln, there arose a desire to conduct regular services so that people could come together to worship and establish a meaningful fellowship with others. Under the able leadership of late Rev. Fr. Korah Varghese, an initiative in this direction was taken by a few members of the community. During this period, services were organized once a month on a regular basis in either Bonn or Köln. To this effect, the community was provided space to arrange liturgical celebrations and other meetings by the Evangelical Church in Germany (EKD) as well as the Roman Catholic Church. Occasionally, services were led by visiting priests and bishops, including late Catholicos Moran Mar Baselios Marthoma Mathews II, late Metropolitan Paulos Mar Gregorios, late Metropolitan Philipose Mar Theophilus, and late Metropolitan Geevarghese Mar Osthathios. Further, Rev. Fr. Geevarghese Pulikkottil (Metropolitan, H.G. Dr. Geevarghese Mar Yulios), Rev. Fr. Dr. Reji Mathews (Dean of Studies, Orthodox Theological Seminary, Kottayam), Rev. Fr. K.T. Varghese (Mount Horeb Asramam, Shastancotta) came to Germany for higher studies and served the community for many years.

Since 2009, the community has been guided and supported by H.G. Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios, the Diocesan Metropolitan, who has regularly appointed priests to take care of the spiritual needs of the community. Moreover, His Grace conducted an episcopal visitation in 2017 to further motivate and strengthen the community in its spiritual journey. In recent years, the community has also received the support and guidance of Rev. Fr. Laiju Mathew and Rev. Fr. Wilson Abraham Poovathumannil.

Since the beginning, the community has regularly celebrated the Feast of St. Gregorios of Parumala. During the early days, around 200 people came together to celebrate the Feast Day with great fanfare. The community also actively participated in a three-day Family Conference that was regularly organized in Germany for approximately 20 years. Furthermore, under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Dr. Reji Mathews, members of the Bonn-Köln congregation enthusiastically participated in the initiative taken by the Orthodox congregations in Germany to build 25 homes for the homeless.

n: Coventry St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds: On November 21st, 2009, St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church Congregation of Coventry was elevated to the prominence of an independent parish ST.MARYS’ INDIAN ORTHODOX CHURCH—by Dr. HG Mathews Mar Thimothios, Metropolitan of the Diocese of the UK, Europe, and Africa. Rev. Tom Jacob delivered active leadership and guidance.

n: Crawley Holy Trinity Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Commenced in 2015. Currently has 60 registered families across Surrey and Sussex counties including Horsham, Haywards Heath, Redhill, Brighton, Worthing, Burgess Hill, and Eastbourne.

n: Dublin St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
The Indian Orthodox worshipping community in Ireland has had its existence from the early 2000s. It was formally declared as the first Parish in the Republic of Ireland in the year 2006 by the late lamented H.G Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios. Since then, under the diligent leadership of clergy and with the efforts of Parishioners, the Parish has made a marked presence in the Republic Ireland.

Dublin, St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church is an active member of ecumenical initiatives such as Irish Council of Churches, Dublin Council of Churches,Dublin City Inter Faith Forum, Kerala Christian Union and Orthodox Church fellowship.

The Parish currently has close to 160 member families along with a large floating community of new migrants and international students. Spiritual Organizations such as Prayer Group, MOMS, Sunday School, Youth, MGOCSM, AMOSS etc. are active.

After celebrating liturgies in the heart of Dublin city for almost 20 years, the newly constructed Church was consecrated on 04 and 05 October 2025.

n: Drogheda St. Peter's and St. Paul's Indian Orthodox Church
ds: St Peter's &St Paul‘s Indian Orthodox Church based in the historic town Drogheda, Ireland was founded in the year 2006 by the prayerful and pioneering initiative of Rev Fr T George with the support of a handful of aspiring faithful living in and around Drogheda and working in the Health Care Sector. The Parish is today rapidly proliferating with a membership of over 50 families. The holy services are conducted at the premises of St Peter's Church of Ireland, Drogheda on every weekend alternating between Saturday at 9am and Sunday at 2pm . The functioning of the spiritual organizations such as the Sunday School, Youth Movement, Vanitha Samajam (Women’s Fellowship) and Prayer Fellowship all contribute to the progress of the parish. The Parish Choir adds flavour to the Divine Liturgy. The Merin George Foundation is a philanthropic activity of the parish, by which, the needs of many a people are met.

n: Galway St. Elias Indian Orthodox Church
ds: Although faithful of the Indian Orthodox Church had been informally gathering in the area for years, the Parish was formally established in 2019 under the able leadership of Fr. Zachariah George (Jessen). Fr. Mathew K Mathew took over as Vicar from August 2021 until January 2025. Following that, Rev. Fr. Joshua Poovathur (Fr. Calvin) served as Vicar from until March 2026.

ds: Dietrich Bonhoeffer Kirche, Oranienburger Str 285, Berlin 13437

n: Germany St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church (Erfurt)
ds: First Holy Qurbana in Erfurt on 10th March 2024 at Brunnenkirche, Erfurt.  Students from Schmalkalden, Jena, Weimer, Ilmenau, Nordhausen, Erfurt come here.

ds: Serbisch-Orthodoxe Kirchengemeinde, Mengendamm 16C, 30177 Hannover

ds: St. Sebald Kirche -  Nürnberg, Von-Soden-Strabe, 28 Altenfurt 90475

n: Hemel Hempstead (London) St. Thomas Indian-Irish Orthodox Church
ds:
The St Thomas’ Indian Orthodox Church, London is a church under the UK, Europe and Africa Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church of India. An appeal was submitted on 15th October 2006 to the Diocesan Bishop to grant permission for a separate parish for the convenience of all IOC members residing in the North London area and its vicinity. St Thomas’ Indian Orthodox Church, London was declared as a parish by the Diocesan Metropolitan, Late Lamented His Grace Dr Thomas Mar Makarios on the 1st of January 2007 and Rev Fr George Joy (Rev Fr Abraham George Cor-Episcopa) was duly appointed as the Vicar of the church.

The newly built St. Thomas’ Indian Orthodox Church, London was consecrated on Friday 31st, August and Saturday 1st, September 2012. The consecration was led by Diocesan Metropolitan HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios and assisted by the Bishops and priests from the Oriental Orthodox family. Rev. Fr. John Varghese Mannancherry served as Vicar from August 2017 to January 2022 and Rev. Fr. Anoop Abraham has been serving as Vicar since February 2022.

n: Julianstown (Co. Meath) St. George Indian Orthodox Church
ds: The St. George Indian Orthodox Congregation Julianstown (Meath) was declared as a Congregation with effect from 05 March 2023 vide pastoral Letter dated 2 March,2023.

n: Leicester St. George Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
The St. George Indian Orthodox Church, Leicester started as a prayer group in the year 2008. Members of Indian Orthodox Church living in and around Leicester, Kettering and Nottingham commenced monthly prayers at the residence of the members under the guidance and leadership Rev. Fr. Tom Jacob. It was in the month of March 2009, that the first Holy Qurbana was celebrated by Fr. Tom Jacob in the Blessed Sacrament RC Church, Braunstone, Leicester. Later, following a request from the members in the area, Diocesan Metropolitan HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios formally declared the Congregation as a Parish on 01 June 2009 with Rev. Fr. Tom Jacob as the priest in charge. He was succeeded by Rev. Fr. Varghese Mathew in August 2014 and re-appointed as vicar in August 2017. Currently Rev. Fr. Binoy C. Joshua has been serving as Vicar since July 2020.

With very humble beginning of just 12 families, the Parish has today grown with 46 registered families. In February of 2019, the Parish was registered as a Charity. Holy Qurbana is celebrated on the first Saturday of every month along with other spiritual activities. From 2018 onwards, the Parish has been congregating at St. Peter’s Church, Glenfield, Leicester, given by Church of England under a spiritual partnership to use for next ten years. Spiritual Organizations such as Sunday School, MGOCSM (Youth), MOMS, etc. actively function in the parish.

n: Liverpool St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds: The first seeds of the Orthodox Syrian Church in Liverpool was laid in October 2003 with the tireless efforts of immigrant community from Kerala. With growing numbers of Congregants, in 2005 the Congregation was officially declared as a Parish by Late Metropolitan Dr Thomas Mar Makarios. St Thomas Indian Orthodox Church, Liverpool provides opportunities for people to worship God. Our worship includes praise, thanksgiving, confession, petition, reading of the Scriptures, and dedication. The Holy Eucharist is offered every first and third Sunday of the month in Malayalam and when there is 5th Sunday in a month the Holy Eucharist will offered in English. The church is registered as a charitable organization, Reg No. 1110650. The spiritual activities include Prayer Meetings, Sunday school, social and charitable activities. The parish with a strength of more than 50 families grows in faith day by day by the grace of God Almighty and the intercession of St Mary, St Thomas and all other saints.

n: London-Brockley St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Cathedral
ds:
St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church, London is the first parish church of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in the United Kingdom. It is considered as the mother church of all other parishes and congregations in the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland. The extensive history of the parish can be traced all the way back to the 1930s with the visits of Abu Alexios of the Bethany monastery (later Bishop Mar Theodosius).

In 1976, parishes outside Kerala were re-organized and grouped under the Diocese of Bombay. The then Diocesan Metropolitan HG. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios on his episcopal visit declared the congregation as a Parish with St. Gregorios of Parumala as its patron saint. Rev. Fr. Abraham Aluckal (now bishop Mar Severios) was appointed as the first vicar of the parish. In the 1979 re-organization of the dioceses, the London Parish came under the Diocese of Delhi and had the privilege of pastoral care of eminent scholar late Dr. Paulos Mar Gregorios who visited the parish on a regular basis. When the new Diocese of Europe, UK and Canada was formed in 1993, this parish came under the jurisdiction of the elite late Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios. With the establishment of the new diocese of UK-Europe and Africa in 2009, HG. Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios took charge as the Metropolitan. The Parish is ever grateful for the relentless services of Rev. Fr Abraham John (late lamented Paulose Mar Pachomios), Rev. Fr. Mathews M. Daniel, Fr. Philipose Thomas (late lamented Philipose Mar Eusebios), Late Ver. Rev. Kuriakose Cor-Episcopa, Rev. Fr. O. Thomas, Rev. Fr. George Kurian (HG Geevarghese Mar Coorilos), Rev. Fr. VM James (HG Yakob Mar Elias), Very Rev. Fr. Thomas Yohannan Ramban, Very Rev. Fr. Skariah Ramban, Rev. Fr. Abraham Thomas, Rev. Fr. John Samuel, Rev. Fr. Thomas John, Rev. Fr. Ninan V. George and Rev. Fr. Aby Philip who served in succession as Vicars of the parish.

The Parish has been fortunate to be able to conduct services in the heart of the great city Of London since 1978 on all Sundays in the beautiful St. Andrew-by-the- wardrobe Church by the generosity of Church of England, and since 2005 in St. Gregorios Church Brockley, London, the first church of the Indian Orthodox Church in UK and all Europe.

n: Lucan St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds: The St. Mary’s Indian Orthodox Church, based in Lucan, West Dublin, is a growing Parish founded in 2009. The Congregation currently meets for worship and fellowship at Lucan Presbyterian Church located in the Lucan Village, County Dublin hardly 20kms away from the Dublin International Airport.

n: Manchester St. George Indian Orthodox Church (Bolton)
ds: The Indian Orthodox Congregation in Manchester had its humble beginning in April 2004 with localized Prayer Meetings held at the residences of various Orthodox families under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Happy Jacob. The first Holy Qurbana was celebrated in November 2004 at the St. Elizabeth's RC Church, Peel Hall. In was on 25th December 2006, during his episcopal visit that the then Diocesan Metropolitan Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios Thirumeni formally declared the congregation as a Parish appointing Rev. Fr. Happy Jacob as the first Vicar. Holy Qurbana is celebrated every Sunday at 9am

n: Mansfield St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
The St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Church , Mansfield is the first Parish of the Indian (Malankara) Orthodox Church in Nottinghamshire, U.K.

The Parish had its humble beginnings as a small prayer fellowship by the name of St. Mary’s with a mere handful of families back in February 2021. By the great blessings of the Almighty and with the permission of the Diocesan Metropolitan HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios, the First Holy Qurbana was celebrated on 24 July 2021 by Rev. Fr. Binoy C. Joshua, who was appointed as priest-in-charge of the spiritual gathering. Later in January 2022, Metropolitan Thimothios visited the fellowship and declared it as a Congregation. The Congregation was elevated to the status of Parish on 28th of May 2023 by the new Diocesan Metropolitan HG Abraham Mar Stephanos.

There are currently 42 member families. The Sunday School has over 40 students and eight teachers. Other spiritual organizations such as Martha Mariam Vanitha Samajam (MMVS), Youth Movement (OCYM) and Prayer Group are also actively involved in the smooth running of the Parish.

Holy Qurbana is celebrated at Sherwood Forest Methodist Church, Big Barn Lane Mansfield, Nottinghamshire NG18 3LJ on the First and Third Saturdays of every month from 9 AM. Spiritual meetings also take place then. Prayer meetings consist of evening prayer, devotional talks and Intercessory prayers.

n: Mullingar St. Stephens Indian Orthodox Church
ds: The Parish in Mullingar, in central Ireland, is the latest to be declared as an independent Parish. In 2013, a few faithful living in and around of the Midlands of the Republic of Ireland commenced a prayer fellowship meeting regularly under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Ninan P Kuriakose. It was only 8 years later in April 2021 that the Congregation was approved and declared as an independent Parish by the Diocesan Metropolitan HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios. The Parish has been dedicated to the blessed memory of the first martyr St. Stephen. Rev. Fr. Ninan P Kuriakose has been appointed as its first Vicar. There are currently twenty families, mostly from the Cavan, Westmeath and Offaly regions registered as members.

n: Nigeria St. Stephen's Indian Orthodox Church (Lagos)
ds:
Although there has been a presence of the faithful of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in Central African countries from the early 1970s, it was never possible to formulate a Congregation as such. However, with the immense desire of the faithful in the region, it was in 2013, that the Congregation was formally founded. The inauguration witnessed a gathering of over 300 members of various Indian Communities. Rev. Fr. Abraham Pangattu, the first Vicar, appointed by Diocesan Metropolitan HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios celebrated the very first Holy Qurbana on 1st September 2013. Rev. Fr. Gigin Baby was appointed Vicar in 2016 and he was succeeded by Rev. Fr. Geevarghese Thampan in 2019.

Rev. Fr. Jibin John Joseph has been leading the Parish since 2021. H.G. Abraham Mar Stephanos visited the parish from Jan 30 to Feb 2 in 2026.

The lay leader of the parish is Jacob John Poovathoor.

n: Northampton St. Dionysius Indian Orthodox Church
ds: St. Dionysious Congregation started as a prayer group in the late 2000s under the guidance of Rev. Fr. Mathew Kuriakose gradually developing into a Congregation by June 2010. It is the only Congregation in the Diocese with ST. Dionysius, the second declared saint of Malankara as its patron saint. Although the Congregation began with a mere eight 8 families, today there are over 20 families as members who gather on the third Saturday of every month to celebrate Holy Qurbana. Rev. Fr. Binoy C. Joshua serves as its Vicar currently. Other spiritual activities like Sunday School, Martha Mariam Samajam, Youth Fellowship as well as other charity events are conducted regularly..

n: Poole St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
As early as 2001, few members of the Malankara (Indian) Orthodox Syrian Church who were health professionals arrived from India to the regions of Poole and Bournemouth. Later on, as their family members joined them, they used to travel to London to attend Holy Eucharistic services.

In 2003, Fr. Abraham Thomas (HG Abraham Mar Stephanos), Vicar at the time of St Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church, London, facilitated to start St Thomas Prayer Fellowship in Poole led by Fr. Varghese Mathew (1st Vicar 2004-2013), which was the inception of the Congregation. The First Holy Eucharist of the congregation was celebrated on 27th September 2003 in the Church of Christ the Saviour, Bournemouth, by Fr. John Mathew, Pallipadu, in the presence of Fr. Abraham Thomas (HG Abraham Mar Stephanos), assisted by late Mr. P C Joseph and attended by about 12 faithful.

The Parish had its blessed inception as a Congregation started with prayer fellowship by dedicated members ever since. Through the years for its spiritual and physical growth. In January 2007, the Congregation was declared as a Parish by Metropolitan of U.K & Canada Diocesan HG. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios of blessed memory.

n: Portsmouth St. George Indian Orthodox Church
ds: The Indian Orthodox congregation in Portsmouth had its humble beginnings towards the end of 2009. The first spiritual gathering was a prayer meeting held on Sunday 13th Dec 2009. This was followed by the first ever Holy Qurbana on Sat 13th March 2010 celebrated by Rev. Fr. Mathews Kuriakose. It was later on 11 September 2010 that the Diocesan Metropolitan HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios proclaimed the Congregation as an independent Parish. Holy Qurbana is currently celebrated on the second Saturday of every month. This is also Followed by Sunday School classes as well as Women’s Fellowship Meetings. The Prayer Group also meets every month on a second Friday in one at member’s homes.

n: Preston St. George Indian Orthodox Church
ds: This Parish is located in the town of Preston in Lancashire, in the North West of England. Following a request from the Indian Orthodox families in Preston and neighboring areas, Diocesan Metropolitan HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios granted permission and appointed Rev. Fr. Happy Jacob to celebrate Holy Qurbana on the third Sunday of every month. Following a request from its members in 2014, the Congregation was formally declared as a Parish and Rev. Fr. Mathews Kuriakose was appointed as the first Vicar. Currently there are 22 families attending the Holy Qurbana and other spiritual activities in the Parish. Spiritual Organizations such as Sunday School, MOMS, etc. function actively in the parish. Rev. Fr. Tom Jacob has been servicing as Vicar from August 2017 onwards.

n: Sheffield St. George Indian Orthodox Church
ds: The St. George Indian Orthodox parish is located in the South Yorkshire County, in the north of England. Sheffield is known as the steel city of UK. The Congregation was formed at Hull, East Yorkshire in April 2005 with St. George as its patron saint and was blessed by Late. Philipose Mar Eusebios who celebrated Holy Qurbana. Thereafter, monthly services were held under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Happy Jacob. Later, due to special circumstance, members started congregating at Sheffield from July 2006 onwards. In December 2006 Late Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios blessed the members with his valuable visit. Under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Varghese John, regular celebration of Holy Qurbana commenced from 2007 onwards. It was later in July 2009, that Diocesan Metropolitan Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios officially declared the congregation as a Parish with Rev. Fr. Varghese John as the first Vicar. The Parish celebrates Holy Liturgy on Sundays once in a month and on special feast days. All Spiritual Organizations as well function fruitfully.

n: South Africa St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church (Gaborone, Botswana)
ds: Note: Gaborone is located in Botswana but falls under the South Africa parish jurisdiction.

n: South Africa St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church (Midrand)
ds:
The St. Thomas Indian Orthodox Church of South Africa traces its roots to the mid-1980s when several aspiring Nasranis came to South Africa in search of better work prospects. A majority of them, being teachers, reached South Africa from other African countries like Nigeria, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Kenya and Lesotho. Facing a lot of hardships owing to the political and social structures, they managed to create a niche for themselves in the local communities of the erstwhile Homelands.

It was only by the mid-1990s that Malayalee Christian communities in various parts across the country were able to gather locally for prayers on a multi-denominational basis. Gradually, as the numbers grew, the Orthodox faithful in these parts took special interest in arranging prayers groups and held occasional worship services. The efforts and services of Fr. Dr. M. O. John, who visited South Africa occasionally proved to be an impetus in the founding and growth of an Orthodox Congregation in Southern Africa. As per the directions of the Late Lamented Metropolitan Thomas Mar Makarios of the erstwhile American Diocese, he was able to conduct Holy Week Services in 1997 and 1998.

The St. Thomas Orthodox Congregation of Southern Africa was officially recognized as a Parish by the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church through a Kalpana issued by Metropolitan Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios dated 23 February 1999. The Parish General Body which met on 4th April 1999 adopted the Constitution of the Parish. It was however only from 2004 onwards that the Congregation was blessed with the presence of a full-time priest, Fr. Jose M. Daniel. He, as well as his successor Fr. Bejoy Varghese served the parish for four years respectively as Asst. Vicars. With the formation of the new Diocese of UK-Europe and Africa in 2009 under the pioneering leadership of HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios, the St. Thomas Congregation entered a new phase in its mission. Fr. Josie John was appointed as the first full time Vicar from 2012 to 2016. Fr. Stanly David James has been serving as Vicar of the Congregation since July 2016.

The Congregation was able to purchase a property in Crowthorne, Midrand (Johannesburg) in 2016 and applied to the municipality in 2017 for the construction of a Church building. A Parsonage Complex as well as guest rooms and a hall was completed in 2019 and blessed by Diocesan Metropolitan HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios during his visit to the Parish for the Holy Week of 2019. By God's grace the Consent for Construction of a Church was approved in August 2019. Following several other delays relating to the Covid Lockdowns and restrictions, all required paperworks relating to Site Development and Building plans were approved by the City of Joburg in February 2022. Construction of the Church commenced with the Laying of the Corner Stone on Sunday 17 April 2022 (Easter Day) and was completed in February 2023. The Service of Holy Consecration of the Church was held on 11/12 February 2023. The Sacraments were led by HG Dr. Mathews Mar Thimothios and HG Abraham Mar Stephanos and was attended by several hundred including priests and representatives from the Coptic Orthodox, Ethiopian Orthodox, Greek Orthodox, Serbian Orthodox, Romanian Orthodox, Emmanuel Marthoma Church Pretoria as well as the SOuth African Council of Churches. The Vice Consul of the Indian Consulate at Johannesburg was also present.

The Malankara Orthodox presence in Southern Africa has indeed witnessed a lot of hardships over the years. The dedication of its members from all quarters along with the services and blessings of several bishops and priests over the years has enabled the Congregation to grow today with almost one hundred and fifty member families spread across over fifteen cities in the Southern African region.

After over 20 years of Christian witnessing, the Congregation was elevated as a Parish by Diocesan Metropolitan HG Abraham Mar Stephanos on June 2023.
